summary: Tested the new 'Practise This Word' feature end to end (backend and frontend) and checked existing features for regressions. Backend: check_practice.py passes against the public URL, and the new pytest file passes 5/5 (status, 401, 400, 422, rate-limit 429). Frontend: the Record → Stop → Play → Analyse flow was driven with an injected fake microphone that plays the cached 'party' clip. Paid member got 100/100 Excellent with the sounds listed under 'Sounds you nailed' and the 'Heard as' line. Saying 'party' against the word 'whole' showed practise-unassessable with a clear reason. Microphone denied showed practise-error with no toast. Nothing was sent to /api/practice/assess until Analyse was pressed. Searching a new word reset the panel. The heteronym 'record' showed the panel without the Hear-reference button. The trial user flow worked, and practising did NOT use up a second trial word. Regressions all pass: logged-out visitors get no panel and see the trial popup; the Scene upload panel renders for a logged-in user; Admin My Dictionary loads and its denied-mic toast is unchanged; the panel looks right on mobile. About 10 Azure assess calls were made in total.

minor.issue: The rate limit is counted before the audio is checked, so empty, too-short or unreadable takes (400/415) count toward the 20-per-hour limit. A user with a flaky mic could hit 429 without a single real assessment. Consider counting only after the audio passes checks.
rate_limit is an in-process memory store: it resets when the backend reloads and is per-worker (seen during the test: a reload cleared the admin's earlier calls). Fine for MVP.

design_issues.screen: Word tab, Practise panel after a take (desktop 1920)
issues: Once 'Record again' and 'Play my take' are shown, 'Hear the American version' wraps onto its own line in the narrow ~535px column. Fine, but slightly uneven.

action_items: Optional: in practice.py, call rate_limit only after the audio-size and ffmpeg checks pass, so rejected takes don't use up a user's hourly allowance
Optional: GET /api/practice/status is fetched again on every PractiseWord mount (seen twice per search). Could be cached at module level.
critical_code_review_comments: practice.py: _to_wav runs ffmpeg via asyncio.to_thread (good, not blocking). The temp dir is cleaned up; no pt-practice-* dirs were left in /tmp after any call.

practice.py: consume_trial runs after a successful Azure call even when the result is unassessable. For a trial user on a word they already unlocked, it does not count again (checked in the DB: trial_word_used stayed at 1).
PractiseWord.jsx: 401/402 are left to the global interceptor in App.js (paywall/login), so no practise-error appears for them. Correct.
useRecorder.js: the onError option is backward compatible; DictionaryBuilder still shows the default toast.
Small point: if a re-record fails because the mic is denied, the previous take and its Analyse button stay visible. That is acceptable.

Fill it from the /api/tts POST response captured when clicking pronounce-play or practise-hear-reference. Set window.__denyMic=true to simulate NotAllowedError. The browser automation tool can read /tmp files, e.g. /tmp/jwt.txt with the admin JWT.
